title: 3320. Count The Number of Winning Sequences

examples.explanation: Bob can beat Alice by making one of the following sequences of moves: "WFW", "FWF", or "WEW". Note that other winning sequences like "WWE" or "EWW" are invalid since Bob cannot make the same move twice in a row.

Bob can beat Alice by making one of the following sequences of moves: "FWFWF", "FWFWE", "FWEFE", "FWEWE", "FEFWF", "FEFWE", "FEFEW", "FEWFE", "WFEFE", "WFEWE", "WEFWF", "WEFWE", "WEFEF", "WEFEW", "WEWFW", "WEWFE", "EWFWE", or "EWEWE".

hints: For 0 < i < n - 1, -n < j < n, and k in {’F’, ‘W’, ‘E’}, let dp[i][j][k] be the number of sequences consisting of the first i moves such that the difference between bob’s points and alice’s point is equal to j and the ith move that Bob played is k.
The answer is the sum of dp[n - 1][j][k]over all j > 0 and over all k.
